articles.title: High Court Rules Against Hopwood DePree in Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A two-day trial in the High Court will determine the future of Hopwood Hall, as Hopwood DePree seeks to reclaim his ancestral home from Rochdale Council.
articles.content_html:
A trial concerning the ownership of Hopwood Hall commenced today in the High Court in Manchester, with Hopwood DePree contesting Rochdale Council's control of the historic manor house. DePree, a descendant of the Hopwood family who built the manor in the 1420s, claims that the council has reneged on an agreement allowing him to purchase the property.

The hall, which has a rich history, was owned by the Hopwood family until 1922 and later sold. It has since served various purposes, including as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s, before falling into disrepair. Rochdale Council acquired the Grade II-listed building and has been responsible for its maintenance.

DePree's legal action follows seven years of collaboration with the council to restore the site, during which he believed he would be able to purchase it. However, in November 2024, the council ended their exclusivity agreement, stating that no commercially viable business model had been presented for the property.

The outcome of this trial could significantly impact the future of Hopwood Hall, as DePree argues that the conditions for the transfer of ownership were met following the granting of planning permission in 2022. The court's decision will determine whether he can reclaim his ancestral home.
